I have been farming this land my whole life. My father farmed it, and his father before him. I know what grows here — the Hebei Plain is good for wheat and corn, nothing else makes sense to me. I have about 8 mu, and I plant winter wheat in October after the rains and summer corn right after the wheat comes off in June. Same land, same rotation, every year. That is how it has always been done here, and it feeds my family.

For wheat, I go to the seed station in town and buy the improved seeds the government recommends — I cannot read the bags but I ask the man there. My neighbor uses them too. I spread fertilizer in two rounds — once when I plant, once when the stalks come up. I irrigate three times: once before planting to wet the soil, once when the plants are shooting up, once when the heads form. I spray once for aphids and once for rust. I use the small rotary tiller my son borrowed money to buy.

For corn in summer, I plant hybrid seed — everyone does now, the yield is much better than the old kind. I put in fertilizer at planting and again when the corn is knee-high. I do not till deeply, I just open furrows. I water twice, usually when it is dry in July and August. I spray for corn borer once.

I do not grow vegetables to sell — just a small patch behind the house for us to eat.
